page: Amazon Web Services m8i.24xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-hypervisor instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. The instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.9 GHz, backed by an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 384.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 4:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Hardware acceleration instruction sets are heavily represented, including AVX-512, AMX tile and int8 execution units, and cryptographic extensions such as VAES and SHA-NI. The instance includes a 40 Gbps baseline network interface, has no local instance storage bundled, and operates without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded throughput and memory capabilities. The instance achieves top-decile scores in PassMark CPU tests (107,013.97), Geekbench multi-core performance (22,352.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (600.69 GB/sec), and Clang software compilation. Memory subsystem testing shows substantial throughput, registering 389.44 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 7,683.86 GB/sec for cached read operations. Microbenchmarks for data services reveal upper-tier throughput, including 172.76 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 155.47 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Natural language model prompt evaluation also achieves top-tier results across 7B and 70B models due to AMX and AVX-512 support, though auto-regressive generation speeds remain moderate without dedicated GPU hardware.

Without integrated local NVMe storage, m8i.24xlarge relies strictly on remote network-attached block storage for persistence, requiring balanced network allocations between data access and service egress. From a qualitative resource-efficiency standpoint, the dense 96-vCPU footprint and high DDR5 memory bandwidth optimize CPU-driven processing pipelines by minimizing core contention and memory bottlenecks. The instance is suited for enterprise web serving tiers, distributed caching layers, large-scale Clang or code build systems, container orchestration hosts, and CPU-based vector search or inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, alongside 480 MB of L3 cache, advanced AMX and AVX-512 extensions, and a 40 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local instance storage or GPU hardware. In benchmarks, the m8i.24xlarge delivers top-tier multi-core compute, software compilation, and memory read speeds, reaching 172.76 million Redis SET operations per second and 155.47 GB/sec static web throughput. Without attached local NVMe, operations depend on external network storage. The hardware profile offers high resource density for enterprise application hosting, in-memory databases, continuous integration build farms, and batch data processing.
